head.b:comment: Indigen World Updates - a custom Blogger theme. Palette and surfaces follow the public website's theme (apps/website/src/styles/comitia-theme.css) in the indigen-world monorepo. Colours, fonts and widths can be changed without editing this file via Blogger, Theme, Customise.
The page's own name comes first so it survives truncation in search results; the homepage gets a descriptive tail instead of the bare blog title.
Home-screen icon. Blogger serves the icon set in Settings, Favicon at /favicon.ico; this adds the 180x180 PNG iOS and Android ask for.

Description. all-head-content already emits og:description and a description meta whenever the page has a search description of its own, so this only fills the gap - the homepage, label and archive views - and never duplicates a tag Blogger has already written. og:url and og:title are Blogger's too; do not repeat them here or scrapers see two of each.

head.b:comment: Site-level structured data. The per-post BlogPosting and BreadcrumbList are built at the foot of the page from the page's own meta tags, so a title with a quote in it can never break the JSON.

Noto Serif Display carries the editorial headlines. Like the rest of the Noto family its latin-ext subset includes the IPA letters Kasem uses (e, o, eng and their tone marks), so a Kasem title never falls back to a second font.
Applies the saved colour scheme before first paint so there is no flash.
Extra CSS from Blogger, Theme, Customise, Advanced, Add CSS lands here.

body.b:comment: Blogger's own navbar is switched off; this theme provides its own header.

b:includable.b:comment: The mark is inline SVG rather than an uploaded header image, so it recolours with the theme. To use your own logo instead, replace the svg below with an img tag pointing at your hosted file.

div.b:comment: Below the nav breakpoint this collapses behind the menu button. It carries inert/aria-hidden while collapsed so its links are not reachable by keyboard or screen reader; the script clears both on open and restores them on close.

body.b:comment: The homepage masthead. The header bar already names the blog, so the headline says what the blog is for instead of repeating the title, and the rail states the three things every reader can expect from a post.

b:if.b:comment: Blogger's image proxy does the resizing, so the browser can pick a width that fits the slot instead of downloading the largest. The lead card is the largest-contentful paint on the index, so it loads eagerly while the rest stay lazy.

div.b:comment: snippet() keeps inline tags, and a cut inside an em leaves the tag open: the browser then re-opens it in every element that follows, which set the sidebar and footer in italics. A template is a parsing boundary, so the fragment is contained; the script copies its plain text into the paragraph.

b:eval.expr: snippet(data:post.body, {length: 165, links: false, linebreaks: false, ellipsis: true})

b:if.b:comment: The byline is the publication, not the Blogger account that pressed Publish. That account's display name belongs to a different blog and was printed on every Indigen World post.

figure.b:comment: The cover is the article's largest-contentful paint, so it loads eagerly and offers narrower files to phones. It is resized without a crop ratio: release covers are 1200x630 art with the headline inside, which a 16:9 crop cut off. The same image opens the post body (it is what makes Blogger choose it as the share card); that copy is hidden.

b:includable.b:comment: Blogger adds Profile and Report Abuse to every new blog whether or not a theme asks for them. Declaring both here keeps them in the sidebar, styled, in place of being appended raw to the bottom of the reading column. This one is hidden by default - a product-updates blog does not need a personal Blogger profile card. Turn it on in Layout if you want one.
Blogger's abuse link. The URL is the fixed one Blogger uses, so this never depends on a data reference that could change under it.
